newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly lower Friday in line with LME copper prices after base metals prices in London drifted back Friday following Thursday's strong gains.
COMEX July was called unchanged to down 0.30 cent from Thursday's close of 111.45 cents a lb after trading from 111.75 to 110.45 cents on ACCESS.
LME copper stocks rose 425 tonnes to 153,350 tonnes Friday, while COMEX copper stocks were down 1,210 short tons Thursday at 43,772 short tons.

While volatility has slipped in the past 10 days, the uptrend in COMEX July copper since mid-April was still intact, traders said, with the July/September spread remaining firmly in backwardation around 3.20 cents a pound.
Union leaders and management held talks Thursday night at the Quebrada Blanca copper mine in Chile to resolve the week-long strike over pay at the pit.

Although there remains the potential for supply disruptions and tightness in the prompt market, by the end of June copper prices should be falling due to rising supply and seasonally weak demand, industry consultants Bloomsbury Minerals Economics (BME) said Thursday.
